newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-VEREINSBANK OPTIMISTIC ON LATVIA, BALTICS.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-VEREINSBANK OPTIMISTIC ON LATVIA, BALTICS.

text.p: German Vereinsbank said on Monday that the number of German companies doing business in Latvia, succesful market reforms and the growth of foreign trade were behind its decision to open a bank branch in Riga.
The Vereinsbank Latvian subsidiary is the first operating branch of a German bank in the Baltics. It is owned by Vereinsbank's unit Vereins und Westbank.
Rolf Kirchfeldt, Vereins- and Westbank board member, noted that from a 60 percent GDP fall in 1992 and the year after, it has now risen by 2.5 percent in 1996.
He told a news conference that the Latvian government expects a growth rate of 4.5 percent, the lat was inflation level was expected at 10 percent or below in 1997.
"Exports to Germany have almost doubled to 109.5 million lats last year from 44.5 million in 1993," Kirschfeldt said.
"After Russia, Germany is now Latvia's second most important trade partner," he said.
More than 200 out of 600 German companies doing business in the Baltics are customers of the Vereinsbank group, he said.
"This alone meant that we had to establish a local office in the Baltic states," he added.
"As the (Baltic) markets get closer, Riga will be the right place for doing business in the region," Kirchfeld told a news conference.
